status_summary: The Made in America Office remains part of OMB: its public website (madeinamerica.gov, undated) describes agency waiver submissions to the office for review and a searchable waiver list, and refers to the current President's Made in America policies. A final FAR rule published 2025-05-12 (90 FR 20220, effective 2025-06-11; proposed 2024-10-23) cut the list of articles presumed nonavailable domestically to 39, so removed items need individual waivers; its preamble says the Councils intend to follow procedures for future list changes that include consultation with the Director of OMB's Made in America Office, a step dropped from the regulatory text, and describes the office sharing market research and giving agencies feedback for consistent waiver use (secs. I.A and IV). EO 14392 (signed 2026-03-13) directs the FTC and procurement agencies on false Made in America claims and does not name the office. No order was found revoking EO 14005; staffing and formal strengthening of the office could not be verified.

timeline.event: FAR final rule published shortening the domestically nonavailable articles list (effective 2025-06-11).
EO 14392 signed: agencies to prioritize enforcement of false Made in America claims and verify origin claims on government-wide contracts.

title: Continue and strengthen the Made in America Office's Buy American work
uncertainties: The madeinamerica.gov page is undated; the date shown for that source is the access date. A Federal Transit Administration notice of proposed Buy America waiver published 2026-06-30 (91 FR 39665), read on federalregister.gov on 2026-10-26, states that FTA submitted the proposed waiver to the Made in America Office at OMB for publication, which shows the office receiving waivers in 2026 and supports continuation but not strengthening. Whether EO 14005 remains in force was not confirmed beyond finding no revocation in the Federal Register API (nine documents from 2025-01-20 mention the office, mostly waiver notices and the FAR overhaul proposal, none revoking it), no revocation or amendment in a further federalregister.gov search on 2026-10-26, and the site still operating; the absence of a search hit is not confirmation that the order is in force. EO 14392 does not name the office, so it is not evidence of strengthening the office itself. The FAR overhaul proposal of 2026-09-18 was not opened, and of the waiver notices only the 2026-06-30 FTA notice was opened. A 2025 or 2026 OMB memo on domestic preferences was not found; a whitehouse.gov search on 2026-10-26 returned only the 2021 and 2022 memoranda (M-21-26, M-22-11). Match is partial because the office's own strengthening is unverified. The FAR rule was proposed on 2024-10-23, before 2025-01-20, and finalized on 2025-05-12; the office consultation appears only in its preamble, not in the FAR text.
